## Design roles

Each part does a job for the person. These are the jobs, as questions the part answers.

<div class="odv-am-rolelist"><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Containment</b> What holds this?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Layering</b> What sits on top?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Hierarchy</b> What do you read first?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Readability</b> Can you read it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Emphasis</b> Where does the eye go?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Meaning</b> What state is it in?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Affordance</b> Can you act on it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Feedback</b> Did it respond?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Focus</b> Where is the keyboard?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Grouping</b> What belongs together?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Reach</b> Can you hit it?</span></div>

## How the decisions reach each part

Each part follows a chain: an answer about the product, the rule it set, the token that carries it, and the value you see. The numbers match the drawing.

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-1-2-3"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox odv-am-pending">Drawn in Figma by the Open DS anatomy plugin; the image is not exported yet.</span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">1</i><i class="odv-am-n">2</i><i class="odv-am-n">3</i><b>Trigger</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="What holds this?">Containment</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you act on it?">Affordance</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you read it?">Readability</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Spacing · How dense is the layout? → Spacious</div><div class="odv-am-why">Room around the text helps reading.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Typography · How large is body text? → Large</div><div class="odv-am-why">Large body text is easy on the eyes.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Shape · What should control corners say? → Rounded</div><div class="odv-am-why">Rounded corners feel friendly.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For field label or column header, use type.label. Don't use type.caption.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Caption is too faint for a label people must read.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For the smallest clickable thing, use size.control.default (touch). Don't use a compact control.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Many readers are on phones.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For corners of buttons and inputs, use radius.control (rounded). Don't use sharp corners.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Rounded corners match the warm reading tone. Sharp corners feel technical next to long text.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>size.control.default</code><span>→</span><code>trigger.height</code><span class="odv-am-val">3rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> size.48</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>space.inset.control-x</code><span>→</span><code>trigger.padding-x</code><span class="odv-am-val">1.25rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> space.20</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>radius.control</code><span>→</span><code>trigger.radius</code><span class="odv-am-val">0.5rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> radius.8: Rounded corners feel friendly.</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.text.muted</code><span>→</span><code>trigger.icon</code><span class="odv-am-val">#61594D · dark #A39A8B</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">The quietest text.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> neutral.600: the quietest text that still reads, 6.9:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div><div><b>Dark</b> neutral.400: the quietest text that still reads, 6.16:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div></div></li></ul></div></section>

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-5"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox odv-am-pending">Drawn in Figma by the Open DS anatomy plugin; the image is not exported yet.</span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">5</i><b>Invalid border</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="What state is it in?">Meaning</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Did it respond?">Feedback</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Color · Which color roles does it need? → Surface, text, action and status</div><div class="odv-am-why">Reading needs few color roles.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For an error message, use color.status.danger and a plain sentence. <section class="odv-am-card" id="part-10"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox odv-am-pending">Drawn in Figma by the Open DS anatomy plugin; the image is not exported yet.</span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">10</i><b>Highlight fill</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="Did it respond?">Feedback</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Where is the keyboard?">Focus</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Accessibility · Which states get their own visible value? → Those and pressed</div><div class="odv-am-why">Pressed gets its own value for touch.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For hover and press feedback, use motion.duration.feedback (moderate). Don't use a fast flash.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Moderate speed feels calm in a slow reading flow. A fast flash feels jumpy.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For keyboard focus, use button/focus-ring at border-width.focus. Don't use removing the outline.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Keyboard users must always see where they are.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.surface.highlight</code><span>→</span><code>item.background.highlight</code><span class="odv-am-val">#F6F2EA · dark #2E2A24</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surface it sits on: darker in light, lighter in dark.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.</div><div><b>Dark</b> neutral.100, one step lighter than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.50), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band on the menu and on cards.</div><div><b>Shares the step with</b> surface.sunken, action.secondary.hover, category.5.subtle, disabled.surface. Changing this pick moves only what reads color.surface.highlight.</div></div></li></ul></div></section>

## For agents

Agents get this same anatomy: every part, its roles, whether it is required, the tokens it reads and the decisions behind them.

- **From an AI agent:** call the `get_anatomy` tool on the Open DS MCP server, with this scheme and `select`.
- **From a terminal:** `npx open-ds anatomy content-first select`
